steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the multidisciplinary capability from September through November 2026 and establish its leadership, decision rights, working model and initial product pipeline. Define how product management, service design, user research, software development, data, integration, architecture, security, accessibility, change and service management will work with King’s Edge product owners and students. Bring the core team into place during November so initial product-definition work can begin in parallel while mobilisation is completed, with the team ready for full delivery from December 2026.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide product governance, institutional prioritisation and alignment between the shared digital capability, King’s Edge demand and the wider Student Experience Hub roadmap.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The development pod may receive conflicting demand or lack authority to make coherent product trade-offs.

existingCapacity.contribution: Set and govern the architecture guardrails, including alignment with the wider technology estate, data foundations, identity, security and integration standards.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may deliver quickly but create capabilities that cannot be integrated, assured or sustained institutionally.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide the governed Azure environment, deployment and operational tooling, platform expertise and routes into existing infrastructure support.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The new development capability could remain dependent on unsupported environments or manual release practices.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide access to institutional data and integration patterns, technical advice and targeted engineering support where the product team must connect to authoritative systems.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The Hub may reproduce data locally or be unable to connect student journeys to authoritative systems.

existingCapacity.role: Security, identity, privacy and accessibility specialists
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide scheduled assurance and specialist decisions throughout design, build and release rather than requiring the team to enter unprioritised service queues.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Assurance issues may emerge late and delay releases or require substantial rework.

existingCapacity.contribution: Define support, incident, change, monitoring, documentation and service-ownership requirements and prepare each product increment for supported live operation.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Products may launch without a credible route into supported business-as-usual operation.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Approximately £201,000 in 2026 prices for November 2026 to June 2027. This assumes four Grade 7-equivalent roles at the current midpoint of £58,649, with employer on-costs comprising 14.5% pension and 15% employer National Insurance above the £5,000 threshold. Future pay awards, recruitment costs, equipment and non-staff technology costs are excluded.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Fund a lean delivery pod comprising two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager. One engineer should be sufficiently senior to provide hands-on technical leadership. The pod creates the development, experience-design and agile-execution capacity that current IT provision does not routinely supply, while drawing on existing IT product, architecture, platform and assurance functions.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: 4.1.4 cannot replatform King’s Edge or replace Accredible in-house, and 4.1.2 will have no reusable product capability through which to build the wider Hub.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the first-year team shape, role profiles and recruitment route in time for recruitment to begin in September 2026.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team will not be available in November and the dependent delivery timeline will slip.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named product, architecture, Azure/DevOps, data, assurance and service-management contributors with protected availability and decision rights.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before the core team begins product definition in November 2026
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Existing IT capacity will remain theoretically available but practically inaccessible through competing demand queues.

enablingConditions.condition: Operate one prioritised product pipeline across 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4, with 4.1.3 holding the staffing capacity and the other deliverables supplying and prioritising demand.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The same team may be double-counted, fragmented across projects or pulled in incompatible directions.

steps.title: Put the Azure delivery foundations into operation
steps.summary: Establish the Azure environments, hosting model, development and deployment pipelines, source-control and release practices, testing and assurance gates, monitoring, logging, recovery, documentation, design and accessibility standards, API and integration conventions, privacy and security controls, and proportionate AI-assurance approach needed to develop student-facing capabilities quickly without creating unsupported or non-compliant prototypes. Begin this work as the core team becomes available during November and complete the delivery foundations by the end of February 2027.

steps.title: Prove the route from prototype to supported service
steps.summary: Use the first King’s Edge releases to run repeated end-to-end delivery cycles: understand and prioritise a need with business users and students, prototype and test a response, develop it within the shared architecture, complete security, accessibility, data and operational assurance, release it into controlled live use, evaluate it, and either harden it for continued service or conclude it cleanly before it creates an unmanaged long-term commitment.

newInvestment.item: Year 2 peak digital product development team
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Approximately £407,000 for 2027/28 in constant 2026 prices. This assumes five Grade 7-equivalent FTE at the current midpoint of £58,649 and 0.5 FTE quality engineering at a Grade 6-equivalent midpoint of £48,773, with 14.5% pension and 15% employer National Insurance above the £5,000 threshold. Future pay awards and non-staff costs are excluded.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Retain the four-FTE first-year pod and add one full-stack or integration engineer plus 0.5 FTE quality engineering and test-automation capacity. This supports concurrent live-service development, wider student-app integration, release assurance and the transition from a single Edge-led backlog towards a broader Hub pipeline.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The team will have insufficient resilience and throughput to operate the live Edge service while integrating wider journeys and improving automated quality assurance.

enablingConditions.condition: Review delivery evidence, the confirmed Hub backlog and support demand in May 2027 before committing the Year 2 uplift.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product leadership with King’s Edge Portfolio Board
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team may either enter Year 2 under-resourced or carry capacity that is not matched to the confirmed product pipeline.

steps.title: Make the product pipeline and support model routine
steps.summary: Confirm the ongoing backlog, prioritisation, discovery, release, support, incident, maintenance, documentation and ownership arrangements for the Student Experience Hub. Establish a reliable delivery cadence, a transparent route for new demand, clear acceptance criteria for moving from experiment to service, and a practical handover or enduring-ownership model for capabilities that have been hardened.

steps.title: Scale the product capability across the student app roadmap
steps.summary: Apply the established operating model and reusable technical foundations to a growing portfolio of student journeys. Increase throughput while preserving continuous user involvement, coherent architecture, shared components, appropriate assurance and sustainable ownership, and use evidence from delivery to refine team roles, governance, methods and the balance between rapid product work and enterprise hardening.

newInvestment.item: Year 3 peak digital product development team
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Approximately £407,000 for 2028/29 in constant 2026 prices, using the same staffing and employer on-cost assumptions as Year 2. Future pay awards and non-staff costs are excluded.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before the 2028/29 staffing plan is fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Continue the peak team of three engineering FTE, one product and experience designer, one agile delivery manager and 0.5 FTE quality engineering through the final intensive year of wider student-app integration, migration, rationalisation and service transition.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Capacity may taper before the wider Hub has completed its principal integration and transition work, shifting unfinished delivery into business as usual.

enablingConditions.condition: Use the Year 2 evidence and confirmed 2028/29 pipeline to validate the duration and composition of the final peak-capacity year.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Year 3 team may not match the balance of engineering, integration, quality and transition work actually required.

steps.title: Embed the team as an enduring institutional capability
steps.summary: Establish the multidisciplinary team, its funding and governance, technical platform, service interfaces and product practices as a sustained institutional capability for continuous improvement of the Student Experience Hub. Ensure the team can respond to new priorities without reverting to disconnected local builds, separate procurements or prototypes that cannot be secured, supported and maintained.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Approximately £263,000 annual recurrent cost in constant 2026 prices. This assumes 3.5 Grade 7-equivalent FTE at the current midpoint of £58,649, with employer on-costs comprising 14.5% pension and 15% employer National Insurance above the £5,000 threshold. Future pay awards and non-staff operating costs are excluded.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before recurrent budgets and organisational structures are fixed for 2029/30
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Recurrent Digital and IT baseline, TBC
newInvestment.rationale: Retain a permanent in-house development core of two full-stack engineers, approximately 0.75 FTE product and experience design and approximately 0.75 FTE agile delivery and product operations. Existing IT product management, architecture, Azure/DevOps, data, assurance and service-management functions continue around this core.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will lose the development capability created through mobilisation and return to procuring, operating or externally commissioning most substantive product change.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm by the end of Year 2 which peak roles remain time-limited and approve the 3.5 FTE recurrent operating model before the final mobilisation year ends.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with institutional investment governance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team may reach the end of mobilisation without an agreed employment, funding or ownership route into business as usual.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm enduring product ownership, service ownership and prioritisation governance for the shared capability and the Student Experience Hub.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the accountable Student Experience Hub sponsor
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The permanent team may exist without clear authority over its backlog, live services or institutional priorities.
